newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom, Daimler to launch traffic navigation system.
newsitem.headline: Telekom, Daimler to launch traffic navigation system.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG and Daimler-Benz AG said Friday they were forming a joint venture to develop navigation systems for cars and trucks using navigation satellites and mobile communications technology.

The deal will combine Deutsche Telekom MobilNet GmbH, the company's mobile communications unit, and Daimler's services division, Debis, to offer services using satellite and mobile telephone systems to guide traffic.
The joint venture plans to offer navigation assistance for big trucking fleets as well as to help direct individual drivers around tie-ups and alert authorities to traffic accidents.
The companies expect to start offering services in the second half of this year and to have three million customers by the year 2000.

They plan to link live data via the Global System for Mobile Communications network and Global Positioning System navigational satellite system to offer services ranging from navigation and first-aid to tracking stolen cars.
The first service the two companies plan to offer is "Tele Aid," which was developed by luxury car maker Mercedes-Benz AG and Debis.

Through a crash sensor installed in the car or a manual switch, paramedics and police will be automatically notified of an accident and the system will be able to locate the car, greatly shortening accident response time.

The next service, planned for the end of the year, will be a piloting system that requires an on-board computer with CD-ROM. The computer will analyse traffic information and using a digital map suggest an alternative route on a flip-up screen to avoid a traffic jam.
